title: Magallanes pomelo (Magallanes suha): Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaTitle: Magallanes pomelo: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaDescription: Magallanes pomelo is a pomelo variety from BPI Baguio (BNCRDC). See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Magallanes is a registered pomelo variety, also sold or known as Magallanes suha or NSIC Pm 02. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council (NSIC) in 2004 as NSIC 2004 Pm 02. BPI Bncrdc bred it. Its record notes a yield of 20 fruits/tree.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Magallanes suha or NSIC Pm 02, this is the same pomelo. The facts below come from the NSIC registry kept by the Bureau of Plant Industry, with notes from its seller and farm sources. Compare it with the others in our [pomelo variety finder](/crop-varieties/pomelo), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [fertilizer for fruit trees](/blog/fertilizer-for-fruit-trees).

blocks.caption: From the NSIC registry and its seller

blocks.text: When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. The mother tree of Magallanes was about 8 years old and about 1.5 meters tall when it was registered. Its record notes a yield of 20 fruits/tree. It bears every year, with fruit in April October. A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
The registry gives no pest or disease ratings for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit pomelo fields most often: [citrus greening](/diseases/citrus-greening), [mealybug](/pests/mealybug), [Oriental fruit fly](/pests/oriental-fruit-fly). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.

A fruit of Magallanes weighs about 753 grams, and its shape is pyriform. The flesh is pink and soft. Its sweetness measured 11.18 degrees Brix, the share of sugar in the juice. Most table fruit tastes sweet from about 12 Brix up. The edible part is 57.16 percent of the fruit. The registry notes its fruiting season as April October, bearing annual.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Fruit:** Pear shaped, about 750 g, light yellow peel, soft, moderately juicy pink flesh, seedless, about 11 Brix.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: the registry's pink, seedless pomelo. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Magallanes pomelo

Davao is the home of suha. Pick a registered selection by flesh color and sweetness, and plant marcotted trees. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Land preparation for fruit trees](/land-preparation/fruit-tree-land-preparation).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is Magallanes suha the same as Magallanes?
items.a: Yes. Magallanes suha is another name for Magallanes, registered as NSIC 2004 Pm 02. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
The record shows a recorded yield of 20 fruits/tree. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of Magallanes?
items.a: Buy grafted, budded or marcotted trees from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, so you get the true variety. Ask your provincial agriculture office for the nearest one.
